context:
Work units are mostly independent but w2/w3 both touch setup.cfg, so
sequence w1 (verification) first, then w2 and w3 together (both edit
setup.cfg - do them in the same change to avoid a broken intermediate
state), then w4 as a separate, optional, independently-landable change.
For w3, actually diff pytest.ini against pytest-ci.ini and pyproject.toml's
dead [tool.pytest.ini_options] before deciding - the dead copy may have
drifted from pytest.ini over time (e.g. its marker list is a different,
possibly stale, subset) and that drift itself is worth noting even if
the block is being deleted, in case any marker only exists in the dead
copy and needs to be ported to the surviving file.
description:
Test-strategy review of packaging/config found three independent, low-risk
hygiene items in the top-level packaging and pytest config files:

1. **Stale `setup.py`.** `pyproject.toml` fully declares the project via
   PEP 621 `[project]` (`name = "benchbox"`, `version = "0.2.1"`, real
   `dependencies`) with `build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"`
   (pyproject.toml:1-7). `setup.py` separately declares
   `version="0.1.0"` and a tiny, wrong `install_requires=["pytest>=6.0.0",
   "pytest-cov>=2.10.0", "pytest-mock>=3.3.0"]` (test-only deps, not the
   real runtime dependency set). Since setuptools' PEP 517 build backend
   reads project metadata from `pyproject.toml`'s `[project]` table when
   present, `setup.py`'s `setup()` call is very likely vestigial for
   `uv build` / wheel builds today - but this must be verified, not
   assumed, before deleting it (see w1).

2. **Dead `setup.cfg` sections.** `setup.cfg` has `[flake8]` and
   `[isort]` sections, but the project's actual lint/format tooling is
   `ruff` (per `pyproject.toml`'s `[dependency-groups] dev` pinning
   `ruff==0.11.13`, and `make lint`/`make format` targets) - flake8 and
   isort are not installed or invoked anywhere. `setup.cfg` also has a
   `[tool:pytest]` section (`testpaths = tests`, a `markers` list) that
   is a SECOND pytest config in addition to `pytest.ini` and
   `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` - a third copy of the
   same settings, silently ignored (see #3).

3. **Three pytest config homes, only one active.** Pytest's config
   discovery picks the first of `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` /
   `setup.cfg` / `tox.ini` it finds in the rootdir, in that priority
   order - `pytest.ini` exists at the repo root, so it always wins
   for a bare `uv run -- python -m pytest` invocation, making
   `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` (lines 424-481) and
   `setup.cfg`'s `[tool:pytest]` section silently dead. This is visibly
   true from `pyproject.toml:426`: `minversion = "0.2.1"` - a copy-paste
   of the PROJECT version into a field pytest interprets as "minimum
   pytest version required," which is meaningless (pytest's real version
   is always >= "0.2.1" as a version-comparison string, so the check
   never fires) and clearly never validated against pytest's actual
   `minversion` semantics because nobody runs this config block.
   There is ALSO a fourth file, `pytest-ci.ini`, which IS actively used -
   explicitly passed via `-c pytest-ci.ini` in `Makefile:316` (`test-ci`)
   and `Makefile:547,550,553,556-558` (`coverage-fast`, `coverage-all`,
   `coverage-html`, `coverage-report`) - so any consolidation plan must
   account for THREE real config surfaces (`pytest.ini` for local/default
   runs, `pytest-ci.ini` for CI/coverage runs via explicit `-c`, and the
   dead `pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg` copies), not two.

Separately (same TODO, same theme): `benchbox/__init__.py`,
`pyproject.toml`'s `[project].version`, `pyproject.toml`'s
`[tool.pytest.ini_options].minversion` (the meaningless copy above),
`README.md`, `docs/README.md`, and `benchbox/utils/VERSION_MANAGEMENT.md`
all separately hardcode `"0.2.1"` - 5 of these 6 are intentionally
tracked and cross-checked by `benchbox/utils/version.py`'s
`check_version_consistency()` (canonical source
`benchbox/__init__.py:17`, doc paths validated via
`_ADDITIONAL_VERSION_PATHS`/`DOCUMENTATION_VERSION_PATHS`,
`version.py:32-37`) - so the runtime-consistency risk is already
mitigated for those 5. The 6th (pytest's stray `minversion`) is NOT
tracked by that checker and is simply meaningless config, addressed by
item 3 above (whichever config file survives should not carry a
project-version-shaped `minversion`). `dynamic = ["version"]` (reading
version from `benchbox/__init__.py` at build time) would collapse the
`[project].version` copy specifically, but is scoped to a decision +
implementation work unit here, not a larger version-management rewrite.

anti_patterns.dont: bundle the dynamic-version decision (w4) into the same PR as the config-file pruning (w1-w3)
anti_patterns.instead: keep w4 as its own PR if adopted.
anti_patterns.why: they're independently risky and independently revertable

anti_patterns.dont: delete pytest-ci.ini or change its content as a side effect of w3
anti_patterns.instead: if w3's decision affects it, do so as an explicit, separately-verified change with each Makefile target re-run.
anti_patterns.why: it's actively used by 5+ Makefile targets

anti_patterns.dont: delete setup.py before verifying uv build output in w1
anti_patterns.instead: verify empirically, don't assume from reading docs alone.
anti_patterns.why: setuptools' PEP 517 backend behavior with a coexisting setup.py + pyproject.toml [project] table can vary by setuptools version

anti_patterns.dont: let setup.cfg's [tool:pytest] markers list silently disappear without checking whether it contains any marker not present in pytest.ini's markers list
anti_patterns.instead: diff the marker lists before deleting.
anti_patterns.why: a marker used in a test file but never declared anywhere becomes a --strict-markers failure

preserves.behavior: Makefile targets test-ci, coverage, coverage-fast, coverage-all, coverage-html, coverage-report continue to work with pytest-ci.ini exactly as before - do not delete or restructure pytest-ci.ini without updating every Makefile reference in the same change.

The xdist safety shim behavior (_benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety.py, loaded via `-p _benchbox_pytest_xdist_safety` in pytest.ini's addopts) - if w3 picks option (A), this line must survive in pytest.ini unchanged; if option (B), it must be carried into pyproject.toml's addopts equivalent exactly.
benchbox/utils/version.py::check_version_consistency() continues to pass for whichever version-string copies remain after w4's decision.
make test-fast selection semantics (whatever marker expression / config file it currently resolves through) - verify with `make test-fast` before and after w3, comparing collected test counts.

scope_rules.path_glob: CI workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml) unless a Makefile target they call changes its config file argument
Makefile targets other than what's needed to keep them pointed at the correct config file name
benchbox/__init__.py (version string stays as the canonical source unless w4 explicitly changes how it's read, not its value)

verifications.command: uv build --wheel && python -c "import zipfile,glob; z=zipfile.ZipFile(sorted(glob.glob('dist/*.whl'))[-1]); print(z.read([n for n in z.namelist() if n.endswith('METADATA')][0]).decode()[:400])"
verifications.description: uv build succeeds and produces correct METADATA before and after setup.py deletion
verifications.expected: Version: 0.2.1 and a real Requires-Dist list, not pytest/pytest-cov/pytest-mock only

verifications.description: make test-fast still selects the same set of tests after config consolidation
verifications.expected: Same pass/fail/collected counts as before the change (compare test session summary line)

verifications.description: make test-ci and coverage targets still work with pytest-ci.ini
verifications.expected: Runs successfully using pytest-ci.ini, no config-not-found errors

verifications.description: No flake8/isort invocation anywhere in CI or Makefile after setup.cfg pruning
verifications.expected: No matches (or only unrelated historical comments)

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "from benchbox.utils.version import check_version_consistency; check_version_consistency()"
verifications.expected: No exception raised / returns a consistent result

work_units.notes:
Before deleting, run `uv build` (or `uv build --wheel`) on the
current tree and inspect the built wheel's METADATA (version,
Requires-Dist) to confirm it reflects `pyproject.toml`'s
`[project]` table (version 0.2.1, real dependency list), NOT
`setup.py`'s version 0.1.0 / test-only install_requires. If
confirmed, delete `setup.py` and re-run `uv build` to prove the
build still succeeds identically afterward (same METADATA, modulo
build timestamp).

RESULT: Confirmed. Before deletion, `uv build --wheel` produced
benchbox-0.2.1-py3-none-any.whl with Version: 0.2.1 and 184
Requires-Dist entries from pyproject.toml's real dependency list
(not setup.py's 3 test-only deps). After deleting setup.py, the
identical build command produced the same wheel filename with an
identical file manifest and Requires-Dist list.

BONUS FINDING: METADATA was NOT byte-identical before/after -
setup.py's coexistence was silently overriding
`requires-python`. Before deletion: `Requires-Python: >=3.10` plus
`Dynamic: requires-python` (setup.py's `python_requires=">=3.10"`
was winning over pyproject.toml's `requires-python =
">=3.10,<3.15"`, silently dropping the `<3.15` upper bound cap).
After deletion: `Requires-Python: <3.15,>=3.10` (correct, matches
pyproject.toml) and `Dynamic: requires-python` is gone. So
setup.py was not purely vestigial - it was shipping a wrong,
wider Python-version constraint in every built wheel. Deleting it
fixes a real (if minor) packaging bug, not just tidies dead code.
work_units.summary: Verify uv build is unaffected by setup.py, then delete it

work_units.notes:
Remove `[flake8]` and `[isort]` from `setup.cfg` (ruff is the active
linter/formatter; grep the repo for any CI step, pre-commit hook, or
Makefile target invoking `flake8` or `isort` first to be certain
nothing depends on them - expected: none). Remove `[tool:pytest]`
from `setup.cfg` as part of w3's config-home decision (don't leave a
fourth pytest config source around even if `pytest.ini` still wins
priority-wise). If `setup.cfg` ends up empty after these removals,
delete the file entirely rather than leaving a zero-content stub.

RESULT: Confirmed `grep -rn 'flake8\|isort' Makefile
.github/workflows/ .pre-commit-config.yaml` returned no matches.
setup.cfg's three sections were `[flake8]`, `[isort]`, and
`[tool:pytest]` (testpaths=tests, python_files=test_*.py, markers:
slow/integration/sqlite only) - removing all three left nothing,
so the file was deleted outright rather than left as an empty
stub. Its 3-marker list (slow, integration, sqlite) is a strict
subset of pytest.ini's markers, so no drift/orphaned-marker risk
from this deletion.
work_units.summary: Prune dead flake8/isort/[tool:pytest] sections from setup.cfg

work_units.notes:
DECISION: Option (A) implemented, as recommended. Deleted
`[tool.pytest.ini_options]` entirely from pyproject.toml (lines
425-481) and `[tool:pytest]` from setup.cfg (folded into w2's
deletion of the whole file). pytest.ini and pytest-ci.ini are
untouched (`git diff pytest.ini pytest-ci.ini` is empty) and
remain the two real config surfaces.

MARKER DRIFT FOUND: pyproject.toml's dead marker list had three
markers NOT present in pytest.ini's list: `datafusion`,
`firebolt`, `databend` (plain form - pytest.ini/pytest-ci.ini only
have `live_databend`, not a bare `databend`, and have no
`datafusion`/`firebolt` markers at all). Grepped
`tests/**/*.py` for `@pytest.mark.(datafusion|firebolt|databend)`
- zero matches (only references are in _project/DONE/*.yaml
planning docs, not actual test files). Since --strict-markers is
only enforced by pytest.ini/pytest-ci.ini (the dead pyproject.toml
block was never read), and no test file uses these markers, this
drift was inert and required no porting before deletion. Noting
it here per the anti_patterns checklist.

setup.cfg's `[tool:pytest]` marker list (slow, integration,
sqlite) is a strict subset of pytest.ini's - no drift there.

Docs check: grepped CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md for
pytest.ini/pyproject.toml/setup.cfg pytest references.
CONTRIBUTING.md:145 says "The default `pytest.ini` is optimized
for quick local feedback. Use the CI profile when you need
coverage..." - already accurate under option (A), no edit needed.
AGENTS.md had no pytest-config-location references to fix.
work_units.summary: Decide and implement the single pytest config home

work_units.notes:
Scope is a DECISION plus (if adopted) a small implementation - not a
broader version-management rewrite. If adopted: set
`dynamic = ["version"]` in `pyproject.toml`'s `[project]` table,
remove the static `version = "0.2.1"` line, and add the
corresponding `[tool.setuptools.dynamic]` section pointing at
`benchbox.__version__` (setuptools supports `attr:
benchbox.__version__` for this). Verify `uv build` and `benchbox
--version` / `benchbox --version-json` still report the correct
version afterward, and that
`benchbox/utils/version.py::check_version_consistency()` still
passes (it may need a small update if it currently reads
`pyproject.toml`'s `[project].version` key directly via
`_PYPROJECT_CACHE` - check `version.py` for exactly how it sources
the "pyproject.toml version" side of its comparison before assuming
no change is needed). If NOT adopted, record the reasoning
(5 tracked copies + 1 runtime checker is judged sufficient
mitigation) as a one-line comment near
`_ADDITIONAL_VERSION_PATHS` in version.py so a future reader doesn't
re-raise the same question without context.

DECISION: NOT adopted. Confirmed by reading version.py:
`get_pyproject_version()` (line ~210) reads `[project].version`
directly out of the tomllib-parsed dict via `_PYPROJECT_CACHE` -
if `[project].version` becomes `dynamic = ["version"]`, that key
is simply absent from the static TOML parse (tomllib doesn't
resolve `[tool.setuptools.dynamic]` attr: pointers - that's a
setuptools build-time behavior, not a TOML-level fact), so
`get_pyproject_version()` would silently start returning None.
That flips "pyproject.toml" from a real tracked source to a
missing one in `check_version_consistency()`'s dev-mode
accounting, which is a regression the fix would have to
compensate for (e.g. teaching version.py to resolve
`attr:` dynamic version pointers itself) - real, non-trivial
version.py surgery for a decision framed as "small". The 5
tracked copies (`benchbox.__init__`, `installed-dist`,
`pyproject.toml`, `README.md`, `docs/README.md`,
`VERSION_MANAGEMENT.md`) plus `check_version_consistency()` are
already a solid drift-detection net for a single low-traffic
version string; collapsing one more copy isn't worth the added
complexity now. The actual motivating problem (pytest's
meaningless `minversion = "0.2.1"` copy-paste) is fully resolved
by w3 deleting the dead `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` block, so
there's no remaining live bug pushing toward adopting dynamic
version. Reasoning recorded as a comment block in
benchbox/utils/version.py directly above
`_ADDITIONAL_VERSION_PATHS` for future readers.
work_units.summary: Decide and optionally implement dynamic = ["version"] to collapse the [project].version literal
